title: Proof of a positive coherent-error threshold for topological quantum codes
abstract: Threshold analyses of quantum error-correcting codes are well established for stochastic error models, in which errors occur randomly with given probabilities. However, errors in actual devices can also be coherent, such as unwanted $Z$ rotations due to imperfect control, which are not captured by stochastic error models. For the surface code, numerical studies have indicated threshold behavior even under coherent errors, but a rigorous proof of threshold existence is lacking. Here we prove that a positive threshold for coherent $Z$-rotation errors exists for quantum low-density parity-check codes with a bounded number of logical qubits, including the surface code and other topological codes. Specifically, we show that the maximum-likelihood Pauli recovery suppresses the entanglement infidelity exponentially in the code distance up to a prefactor linear in the number of physical qubits whenever the rotation angles lie below a constant that is independent of the code size. The proof combines Fourier analysis to retain the interference among the amplitudes of coherent errors with the cluster expansion of abstract polymer models. Our results expand the theoretical foundation of quantum error correction and offer a statistical-mechanical description of quantum error correction beyond stochastic errors.
summary: This paper establishes a theoretical proof for a positive error threshold in topological quantum codes when facing coherent errors, a significant advance over previous stochastic-only models. By combining Fourier analysis and polymer model techniques, the authors show that the logical error rate decays exponentially with code distance for Z-rotation errors. This work deepens the theoretical understanding of quantum error correction in realistic, non-stochastic noise environments.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously prove the existence of a positive error threshold for topological quantum codes when subjected to coherent errors, extending previous results limited to stochastic error models.
main_result: It proves that a positive threshold exists for coherent Z-rotation errors for CSS QLDPC codes, showing that the entanglement infidelity is suppressed exponentially with code distance.
method: The proof combines Fourier analysis to handle interference effects from coherent errors with the cluster expansion technique applied to abstract polymer models.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is quantum error correction (QEC) applied to topological stabilizer codes, such as the surface code, defined on local lattices. The errors considered are coherent Z-rotation errors.
key_observables: Entanglement infidelity of the recovered logical information, and the existence of a positive error threshold.
important_parameters: Code distance ($d$), the magnitude of the coherent rotation angles ($	heta_j$), and the number of physical qubits ($n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the syndrome measurement is performed in a noiseless way (code-capacity setting) and that the rotation angles are bounded by a constant independent of code size.
paper_structure: The paper builds from preliminaries (stabilizer codes, CSS codes, QLDPC codes, Fourier analysis) to derive the main theorem using advanced mathematical tools like Fourier analysis and the cluster expansion.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding fault tolerance beyond the standard assumption of independent, stochastic errors, which is crucial for modeling real-world quantum hardware imperfections.
